title: Microsoft is killing its great tasks app in favor of its worse tasks app
snippet: To Do was a nice app while it lasted. | Image: Microsoft In 2015 Microsoft acquired a to-do list app called Wunderlist, for a price rumored to be as high as $200 million. Wunderlist fans were worried that Microsoft would make their beloved app soulless and corporate, or worse, hide it behind some convoluted enterprise subscription. But against all odds, Microsoft was a good steward: The app became Microsoft To Do, but it remained a useful and powerful way for people to manage their tasks across all platforms. Now Microsoft is pulling the rug. Buried deep in a blog post about "unified tasks and plans for Copilot and Microsoft 365" is the news that the To Do apps will "retire" on June 30th, 2027. T … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
In 2015 Microsoft acquired a to-do list app called Wunderlist, for a price rumored to be as high as $200 million. Wunderlist fans were worried that Microsoft would make their beloved app soulless and corporate, or worse, hide it behind some convoluted enterprise subscription. But against all odds, Microsoft was a good steward: The app became Microsoft To Do, but it remained a useful and powerful way for people to manage their tasks across all platforms.

Now Microsoft is pulling the rug. Buried deep in a blog post about “unified tasks and plans for Copilot and Microsoft 365” is the news that the To Do apps will “retire” on June 30th, 2027. The transition will be painful: Starting next summer, business users will need to use the Planner app for their tasks, but Microsoft won’t migrate their tasks automatically. And personal users, well, don’t let the door hit you. “Customers using personal Microsoft accounts will need to choose another app,” the blog post reads.

From a certain strategic standpoint, you can almost see how this makes sense. (Microsoft hasn’t responded to a request for comment.) It’s definitely true that Microsoft’s task- and project-management offerings are too complicated; To Do and Planner have some overlapping features, and you can use a half-dozen different Microsoft apps to manage your daily tasks. Microsoft has been hinting at bringing everything under the Planner banner for some time, and as Microsoft tries to foist Copilot upon everything you do at work, bringing all that stuff into one place makes more sense.

(“More sense” may be relative, though. When your blog post contains sentences like, “Additionally, this unified platform makes accessing Planner through Copilot, Cowork and Autopilot easier because it’s all part of Work IQ,” you still have some work to do.)

It’s also yet another sign that Microsoft is simply giving up on the idea of making software that people use outside of work. Planner isn’t available through a personal or family Microsoft 365 account, so you can’t switch if you want to. Not that you necessarily would: Lots of people liked To Do specifically because it was a list of tasks, not a project management platform. Planner is a business tool for business users, administered by IT professionals and monitored by big bosses.

Planner is also, in many ways, just not as good a platform. It doesn’t have a dedicated desktop app — you’re meant to use it on the web, or through Teams or Outlook — and is missing some of To Do’s useful syncing and sharing features. Microsoft is not promising to spend the next six months closing those gaps, or even offering to help people export their data and move on. The company is simply getting all the way out of the business of helping regular people manage their days, and leaving users in the lurch.

If you’re suddenly shopping for a new to-do list, the good news is there are plenty of good options. Todoist and TickTick are the two stalwarts of the space, and they offer much of the same ubiquity and simplicity as To Do (though I agree with all the commenters on Reddit and Microsoft’s blog, who say To Do’s interface was better than either one.) Google Tasks is being integrated across Google’s own office suite. The vibe coding revolution has also persuaded approximately every person on the internet to build their own to-do app, so you have lots to choose from. At this point, there’s seemingly only one company left that doesn’t want you managing your days and tasks in its systems, and it’s Microsoft.

title: Apple among the companies facing pressure from US senators over ‘nudify’ apps [U: Apple responds]
snippet: The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable users to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow users to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed users to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

Senate Democrats demand answers

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”

From the report:

A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of New Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta said they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same issues.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

From The Guardian’s report:

Keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, said that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

Update, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said:

“We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for users. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The company added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the company said does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

As for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

Apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The company said that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

title: YouTube Music rolling out corner Gemini icon to launch Ask Music
snippet: Besides removing the Samples tab, YouTube Music for Android and iOS is rolling out instant access to Ask Music with a new Gemini icon in the top-right corner. more…
fullText:
Besides removing the Samples tab, YouTube Music for Android and iOS is rolling out instant access to Ask Music with a new Gemini icon in the top-right corner.

The Gemini spark appears on almost every screen in the app, including the Home feed, Library tab, Now Playing, albums, and playlists. It matches Gemini in Gmail and other Workspace apps online, as well as Google Messages in a future update.

Tapping launches Ask Music, which requires a YouTube Premium or Music Premium subscription, as a fullscreen sheet. This chatbot lets you create a mix, discover artists, find podcasts, build a playlist, and ask about your listening history. You can also “customize your queue or dive deeper into artist lore.” In addition to the text field, there’s also voice input.

Ask Music launched in 2024 and was previously accessed from a card in the Home feed.

	

The new access point has been rolling out in recent days as a server-side update, and we’re seeing it on many more devices as of today. YouTube previewed this addition back in September along with “your podcast lineup.” This “personalized AI-audio guide” appears in the Podcasts feed to provide a “quick, weekly spoken preview of recommended shows and digs into why you’ll like them, before jumping into the suggested episodes.”

title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit
snippet: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit, rather than reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. The short answer is AI, but not in the way you might expect.
fullText:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff.

Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI.

The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit.

“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained.

For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.”

He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.”

He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.”

But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company, didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’”

When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast, Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.”

He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.”

In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. Elsewhere.

title: Zane Lowe shares Apple Music Radio audience numbers, recalls ‘crickets’ in the early days
snippet: In a new interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
In a new interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details.

Apple Music Radio top 50 million monthly listeners

Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.

In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue said Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.

Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, however, has now offered a more concrete figure, revealing that the service reaches over 50 million unique listeners every month:

We were never, you know, delusional enough to assume we were going to get a huge audience overnight. We’d have to build it like anyone else would have to build anything. But we’ve just got to a point in our 11 years on where we now, overall, reach over 50 million unique listeners a month, which is a really large number for us, and it’s growing exponentially and really fast.

The revelation came in a wide-ranging interview published today with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, where Lowe discussed Apple Music Radio’s early struggles, its approach to supporting emerging artists, and why human curation remains central to the service.

When discussing the early days at Apple Music, Lowe recalled:

When we started the radio here, I didn’t have access or opportunity with a lot of the artists that I built relationships with from the BBC because we were unproven. And I came over here thinking, “Well, I’ve got Jimmy Iovine over here, and I’ve got Apple over here and I feel unstoppable, and who’s not going to want to come and launch this thing with us?” But it was kind of crickets… As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it. Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch. And number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a big way on new and emerging artists.

He also mentioned some of the first artists Apple Music Radio supported, including Billie Eilish with “Ocean Eyes,” Khalid with American Teen, and Bryson Tiller with his first song.

At the time, Lowe noted, these artists were just getting started, and supporting emerging talent became a defining part of Apple Music Radio’s approach, one that continues to this day:

The really cool number is on our radio network. We played — this year alone — over 6,500 individual artists, which is not a commercial radio model. [Other radio networks’] playlists are very small, and the amount of plays is very great. Our playlist is gigantic. We play a lot of different artists, and over half of those 6,500 artists we’ve played in one year are new or emerging. So, think about 3,300 artists, roughly, getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album…It’s proof of concept. It’s great.

Still on the subject of the early days at Apple Music, Lowe said “it was very clear [from the start] that that was very important to everybody who was responsible for bringing Apple Music to life,” adding that “serving artists and the artistic community in a way that is of most value and of most service” still drives “a lot of the decision-making” at the platform.

When the conversation turned to Apple Music’s recent rebranding, which introduced a new logo physically created using sound waves from a composition by Fred again.., Lowe said he couldn’t speak to the decisions behind it, but stressed the human element and the creative process that went into it:

We could have created that in a way that could utilize all of the tech available. We could type that into a prompt. But at the end of the day, seeing how it’s made is so much more additionally inspiring than just seeing it. It speaks to, I think, what we try to do here, which is, we love the process of what we do, and the result is a byproduct of getting to do it and loving to do it.

The issue of algorithms also came up when Lowe discussed Apple Music’s approach to music discovery, with the executive emphasizing the importance of human curation over automated recommendations:

Well, we don’t want to say that too loudly, because someone could be like, “Wait a minute, we could cut costs here? Man, how did we not think of that!” Look, I mean, jokes aside, we’ve been incredibly fortunate, and I’ve been incredibly fortunate to take that step from the BBC into a company and to work with people that value exactly what it is you’re describing: this idea of place and this experience of sharing things with each other, and how meaningful it is when someone shares a record with you and it comes with context. It’s a gift…

title: Which Laptops Last the Longest? Check Out the Laptops I’ve Tested With the Best Battery Life
snippet: As part of our video series Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, I share laptop recommendations and explain why battery life surged in 2026.
fullText:
I can almost guarantee that your next laptop will run longer on battery power than whatever you’re currently using. We’ve seen a huge leap in laptop battery life in recent years, to the point where getting 20 or more hours on a single charge isn’t uncommon. This year alone, the average battery life of the laptops we’ve tested at CNET has increased by more than five hours. And it’s nearly doubled since the start of the decade.

With many of today’s laptops, you can leave the charger at home for days at a time. The longest-lasting laptop I tested this year lasted more than 34 hours! 

This increase in battery life is one of the biggest stories in laptops this year. In the laptop episode of our video series Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, I explain what’s behind this surge in battery life and highlight some of the laptops that lasted the longest in testing.

Plus, my colleagues Kyle Kucharski from ZDNET and Joe Osborne from PCMag share their own holiday laptop picks. Kyle looks at Apple’s entry-level MacBook Neo and its imitators, and Joe breaks down what to look for in a budget gaming laptop.

Today’s laptops last longer

Unlike raw performance, where the more you spend, the more you get, lengthy battery life can be found just as easily in a budget laptop as in an expensive, high-end powerhouse. And, in fact, less powerful components and lower screen resolutions can give cheaper laptops an edge in battery life.

The biggest factor behind longer battery life in laptops is the advancement in mobile processors. They’ve become much more power efficient, and in the case of Apple’s and Qualcomm’s chips, they’re based on an architecture other than the traditional x86 instruction set that’s been at the heart of Intel processors since the dawn of the PC era.

Apple’s run of battery-life winners started when it shifted from Intel processors to its own M-series chips. Apple’s M-series processors are based on the Arm architecture, a power-efficient chip architecture found in phones and tablets. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X-series processors are also Arm-based, and they can be found in the two longest-running laptops we’ve tested: the HP OmniBook 3 16 and OmniBook 5 14. The OmniBook 3 16’s record-setting battery performance earned it a CNET Lab Award for longest battery life.

Powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon X processor, HP’s OmniBook 3 16 ran for more than 34 hours in testing to set the record for the laptop with the longest battery life.Matt Elliott/CNET

Intel has made huge strides in processor efficiency with its last two generations of chips: the Core Ultra 200 series developed under the name Lunar Lake, and the Core Ultra 300 series, also known as Panther Lake. Last year, the Lenovo Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition became the first Intel laptop to last longer than a day, running for 25 hours, 45 minutes in testing. It’s still the longest-running Intel laptop we’ve tested, but the MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI Plus with Intel’s next-gen Core Ultra X7 358H processor came close with a time of 25 hours, 18 minutes.

Read more: Laptops With the Best Battery Life

Whether Arm or x86, there are two more reasons behind greater processor efficiency and longer laptop battery life. For one, the size of a processor shrinks with every generation. The smaller a processor is and the more tightly packed its components are, the less power is required to flip its tinier transistors on and off. For another, today’s mobile processors feature more flexible designs with a mix of performance and efficiency cores. A processor engages its higher-performance cores only when needed, using the efficiency cores for as many general, everyday tasks as possible, so your laptop stays cool and quiet and runs longer.

For more, you can read my Labs exclusive on the huge increase in laptop battery life this year and check out the video above for my holiday laptop picks and those from my colleagues.

title: You can now assign Gemini ‘tasks’ for free in six countries
snippet: Starting today, the Gemini app’s “tasks” feature, previously known as Spark, is now available for free users after requiring AI Pro in the past. more…
fullText:
Starting today, the Gemini app’s “tasks” feature, previously known as Spark, is now available for free users after requiring AI Pro in the past.

Google previously referred to this capability as a 24/7 personal agent before integrating directly into the main Gemini app experience in October. Above the prompt box on mobile (or below on the web), you’ll see “Chat” and “Task.” The first option is the existing chatbot, while the latter lets you “hand off even more tasks to Gemini.”

With tasks, Google’s “goal is for Gemini to save you time and money.” Google shared use cases like:

“Last month it saved us real money after we got hit with a surprise $389 electric bill. I gave Gemini permission to access our utility portal with the new Google Password Manager integration and asked for it to analyze our past billing statements in my email. Gemini worked for a few minutes, and then nailed it. The primary culprit was our heat pump, which it turns out was kicking on around 4 p.m., right in the middle of peak pricing. My wife and I never would have caught that digging through the PDFs and emails ourselves.”

“For our upcoming holiday trip back to Oklahoma, I recently asked Gemini to give me the best options for a USB-C charger. Gemini quickly compared chargers thanks to Google’s Shopping Graph, asked me follow-up questions about the wattage and color, and then helped me check out using the new Google Pay integration. The best part: it also found a discount code so I saved an extra $10. Done.”

With today’s announcement, Google is emphasizing that “Gemini is your best choice as a personal assistant because [your emails, calendar, passwords, photos, files, and payment cards] already lives at Google securely, and you don’t have to send it elsewhere.”

	

Behind the scenes, Gemini tasks work in your own “hardware-isolated virtual machine” that’s sandboxed and has protections against prompt injection, while leveraging Google Safe Browsing when browsing the web.

Related: You can now Email and Text (via Google Messages, iMessage) with Gemini 

Other safety features include having you confirm purchases and asking “clarifying questions if an instruction is ambiguous.” 

Powered by the new Hydrogen model, free Gemini tasks are available in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India.

title: New gradient icons roll out to Google Messages & Contacts
snippet: Google this week completed the rollout of its new gradient icons with updates for Messages and Contacts. more…
fullText:
Google this week completed the rollout of its new gradient icons with updates for Messages and Contacts.

The icon shapes remain the same for all three communication apps, though they are slightly larger and better fill the circular backgrounds. Contacts is still a head and body, while Messages remains overlapping chat bubbles and Phone a handset. This redesign is not particularly disruptive.

A lighter shade of blue is leveraged, while all feature a gradient effect. This results in the logos feeling less heavy and a bit more modern. 

Google describes the new Messages icon as “sharper, crisper, and clearer than ever before.” The SMS/RCS client did not roll out any other changes with the logo redesign this week. The big homepage redesign is still in the beta channel.

	

Google Contacts was the last Android icon to be refreshed, with version 4.92.26.x rolling out on Wednesday evening. The Phone by Google update rolled out on Monday to stable users.

It took two weeks from announcement to full availability across the three apps.

title: Motorola Razr Fold finally gets its Android 17 update – hopefully the next 7 years go faster
snippet: Motorola has kicked off its Android 17 rollout for the Razr Fold, marking the first major update for the company’s first book-style foldable, and the start of a potentially interest 7 years of software support. more…
fullText:
Motorola has kicked off its Android 17 rollout for the Razr Fold, marking the first major update for the company’s first book-style foldable, and the start of a potentially interest 7 years of software support.

The Motorola Razr Fold launched with Android 16 back in May 2026, and it remains a really good option for those looking to pick up a book-style foldable in the US. On top of solid specs across the board, it also carries the promise of 7 years of software support, something that few other Moto devices can tout.

But nowhere was it promises that Motorola would speed things up at all. A little over 3 months after Motorola announced the update and several weeks after other Motorola devices were updated to Android 17, the Motorola Razr Fold is finally getting its own Android 17 update. 

Rolling out now, Android 17 for the Razr Fold is a 4.15GB~ update that appears to be available at least somewhat broadly. Reports are popping up on Reddit including one report from the EU (Hungary, specifically), with another user apparently in a Spanish-speaking region also seeing the update. 

	

Motorola’s changelog explains:

Enjoy a fresh, expressive design

Reduce clutter with smarter notifications

Multitask faster and keep more apps accessible at once

Stay extra secure with enhanced protection and controls

We’re still waiting to see if the update is available in the US (there’s a backlog of updates on our unit), but it’s certainly an update to look forward to. Apparently, Motorola finally fixed a weird UI issue that affected the Telegram app, something we ran into when using the device earlier this year. 

It’s great to see the update out, but it’s noteworthy that Motorola is not setting a particularly encouraging precedent here. Razr Fold is one of the company’s first devices to be promised 7 years of OS updates and software support, and its flagship-tier status certainly would have most expecting it to be updated ahead of some of Motorola’s more affordable, lower-tier devices that were updated over a month ago. Whatever the case, hopefully Motorola will speed things up over the next few years, especially with its $1,600 flagship Signature 27 on the horizon with the same software promises.

title: VSCO launches its first native Mac photo editor with RAW support, batch editing, more
snippet: VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the company’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside new features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the company’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside new features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details.

VSCO comes to the Mac

Professional and amateur photographers just got a new alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the company’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.

More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the company’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing users to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.

It also supports keyboard shortcuts similar to those found in other popular photo editors, making it easier for photographers familiar with those apps to get started.

Here’s Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, on today’s launch:

“Photographers deserve tools built around how they actually work. […] 75% of VSCO Pro members have used our presets in the last six months. Now those looks live on the desktop, with one connected workflow from camera to client delivery and nothing getting in the way.

The first thing users will notice, and then continue to notice when using VSCO Studio Pro, is how fast it is. From changing the grid size, to sorting images, to applying presets by rolling the cursor over each of the 200+ presets, pretty much everything about VSCO Studio Pro feels as real-time and instant as it can be when dealing with large numbers of images.

As for importing photos, VSCO Studio Pro supports Apple Photos, local folders, SD cards, and external drives, and offers RAW compatibility with more than 800 cameras from 20 brands. Users can also choose whether to work with files in their original location or copy them elsewhere.

Under the hood, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop combines Apple’s Core Image RAW processing with the company’s own Reflex image processing engine, which handles presets and editing adjustments.

Batch editing in VSCO Studio Pro Desktop can handle anywhere from two to 500 images at once, which is great for quickly applying the same preset or film-inspired look (including Kodak Portra, Kodachrome, Fujifilm Velvia, and Kodak Tri-X), or making adjustments to an entire set of photos simultaneously, with changes appearing across all selected images in real time.

And speaking of presets, VSCO Studio Pro packs an exclusive one called IOE1 Pro, developed with photographer Joe Greer. IOE1 Pro, as well as VSCO’s other presets, allow users to adjust the strength, color, tone, and contrast, further helping them fine-tune each look to their liking.

VSCO Studio Pro’s editing tools include the usual suspects photographers might expect from photo editing software, including exposure, contrast, fade, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, skin tone, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, lightness, sharpening, clarity, vignetting, and grain adjustments for strength, size, and color.

VSCO is also working to expand its toolset to include bloom and halation effects, curves, masks, and a remove tool for users looking for more control over their edits and to make more precise, localized adjustments to their images.

Also in the works are new organizational features, including projects for managing groups of photos, as well as culling tools that will allow users to rate images with stars and mark them as accepted or rejected, making it easier to sort through large photo collections.

Once users are happy with their adjustments, they can export their photos individually or in batches, choosing the file name, format, resolution, and compression quality. VSCO Studio Pro also offers resizing presets for web, social media, and client delivery, as well as the option to save the finished images to a folder of their choice.

And speaking of client delivery, users can publish their edited photos directly to VSCO Galleries, allowing them to share full-resolution images without having to export them and upload them separately elsewhere.

VSCO Studio Pro Desktop is available today as a free download for Apple Silicon Macs, with full feature access requiring a VSCO Pro membership, starting at $4.99 per month or $59.99 per year, or a VSCO One membership. You can see it in action below:

fullText:
The monthly “Google System Release Notes” primarily detail what’s new in Play services, Play Store, and Play system update across Android phones/tablets, Wear OS, Google/Android TV, Auto, and PC. Some features apply to end users, while others are aimed at developers.

The following first-party apps comprise the “Google System”:

Android AICore: Search the “All apps” list in Settings and open App info for the version number

Adaptive Connectivity Services: App info

Android Developer Verifier: App info

Android Pulse: App info

Android System Intelligence: App info

Android System Key Verifier: App info

Android System SafetyCore: App info

Android System WebView: App info

Android TV Core Services

Device Health Services: App info

Google Partner Setup: App info

Google Play Protect Service: App info

Google Play services: App info

Google Play Services for AR: App info

Google Play Store: App info

Google Play system update: Settings > About phone > Android version

Private Compute Services: App info

Quick Share Extension: App info

Search Engine Selector: App info

Settings Services: App info

SIM Manager: App info

System parental controls: App info

To update, open the Settings app > tap your name at the very top for “Google services” (on Pixel) > All services tab > Privacy & security > System services.

A feature appearing in the changelog does not mean it’s widely available. Some capabilities take months to fully launch.

	

Google Play services v26.45 (2026-11-16)

Account Management

[Phone] With updates to storage management, you can track your cleanup progress, quickly review large files by swiping to keep or delete them, and easily see which Google Account you are managing.

Developer Services

[Auto] New developer features for Google and third party app developers to support Maps related processes in their apps.

Device Connectivity

[Auto] This update enables settings for cross-device experiences between your car and your Android devices.

Health & Fitness

[Phone, Wear] This update lets your watch use your phone’s GNSS to track location during outdoor workouts and helps conserve watch battery life when your phone isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

Wallet

[Phone, Wear] New developer features for Google and third party app developers to support Digital Wallet & Payments related processes in their apps.

[Phone] Bug fixes for Wallet related services.

Google Play Store v54.1 (2026-11-16)

[Phone] You can now view a large and immersive preview of a watch face on the app details page to help you choose the right design.

[Phone] With this update, Google Play now suggests relevant apps when your search returns no results.

[Phone] You can now use an on-screen game controller in supported Android games with Pixel virtual gamepad when your Pixel Fold is open.

Related: Android 17 gives foldables the virtual gamepad they’ve always deserved

Android WebView v158 (2026-11-09)

Improvements to security and privacy and updates for bug fixes.

New developer features for Google & 3rd party app developers to support functionality related to displaying web content in their apps.

Important: Some features may be experimental and available to certain users.

Google Play services v26.44 (2026-11-09)

Developer Services

[Auto, Phone, TV, Wear] You can now use an API to query the age range of the device user.

[Phone] This update makes it easier to participate in cross-device experiences.

System Management

[Auto, PC, Phone, TV, Wear] Updates to system management services that improve Stability.

[Auto] Updates to system management services that improve Device Performance.

Utilities

[Auto, PC, Phone, TV, Wear] New developer features for Google and third party app developers to support Utilities related processes in their apps.

Wallet

[Phone] You can now use Traveler QR in Google Wallet.

[Phone] You can now add Matter Aliro-compatible single-family residential keys to Google Wallet with Google Home.

Google Play Store v54.0 (2026-11-09)

[Phone] You can now find contextual AI suggestion chips on Google Play single-event LiveOp Event Details Pages.

[Phone] Delivers real-time updates of player sign-in/sign-out state for Play Games Services to Play Store.

[Phone] This update allows select users to receive Play Points promotions for new subscriptions on the Play Store.

Google Play services v26.43 (2026-11-02)

Account Management

[Phone] You can now access the Android Family Hub, a dedicated space for family management tools in Android Settings.

Developer Services

[Phone] New developer features for Google and third party app developers to support Location & Context related processes in their apps.

Device Connectivity

[Auto, Phone, TV] This update adds more quality logs for device connectivity.

[PC, Phone] Automatic backing up photos/videos from an Android to Windows using Quick Share feature.

Safety & Emergency

[Phone] Bug fixes for Safety & Emergency related services.

Security & Privacy

[Phone] Google Password Manager now allows you to manually choose which credentials to keep when importing conflicting passwords and passkeys.

System Management

[Auto, Phone] Updates to system management services that improve Battery Life, Device Connectivity, Device Performance, Privacy, Security, Stability, and Updatability.

Wallet

[Phone] Updates to Wallet loyalty cards.

[Phone] Bug fixes for Wallet related services.

Google Play Store v53.9 (2026-11-02)

[PC, Phone] With this update, you’ll get a reminder if Play Protect stays off for a while.

[Phone] With new at-a-glance highlights on game detail pages, you can quickly find gameplay style, review summaries, and gaming community activity before you install a game.

title: Chrome 157 for Googlebook rolling out with 27 new features, improvements
snippet: Chrome 157 widely rolled out last week, and Google is now sharing the extensive changelog for Googlebook OS. more…
fullText:
Chrome 157 widely rolled out last week, and Google is now sharing the extensive changelog for Googlebook OS.

There are five new features for the browser in version 157:

Auto-Expand Vertical Tabs on Hover: Hovering over a collapsed vertical tab rail with a mouse or trackpad now temporarily expands it as an overlay so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups, and retracts when you move your cursor away. This is enabled by default and can be toggled off or on in Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover” or by right-clicking the vertical tab rail.

Resizable Vertical Tab Bar: You can now manually resize the vertical tab bar to view longer page titles without truncation, and Chrome remembers your custom width across browser restarts and new windows (supported when “Auto expand tabs on hover” is turned off).

Direct URLs and Back/Forward History for Settings: Individual Chrome Settings subpages now have direct web addresses (such as chrome://settings/appearance or chrome://settings/privacy) that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly. Navigating between Settings subpages also works with Chrome’s Back and Forward buttons.

Tab Sharing Controls Bar: When sharing a browser tab in video calls (such as Google Meet), Chrome now displays a persistent control bar at the top of the window to “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

“Save As” System File Dialog: The system “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for explicit menu save actions (such as “Save link as…”, “Save image as…”, and “Save page as…”), letting you rename files and choose a destination folder, including Google Drive or external storage.

This is followed by 22 improvements, especially for the Bookmarks Bar, Vertical Tabs, and Address Bar. Of note is the “standard desktop text-editing menu” when right-clicking the address bar.

Bookmarks Bar Right-Click Menu: Context menus now open properly when right-clicking on the bookmarks bar or bookmark folders.

Bookmarks Bar in Fullscreen: Switching tabs in fullscreen mode while vertical tabs are enabled now keeps the bookmarks bar visible.

Bookmarks Bar During Screen Sharing: Clicking on bookmark items on the bookmarks bar now responds normally while presenting or sharing your screen in Google Meet.

Pinned Tab Hover Cards: Hovering over a pinned tab consistently displays the tab preview hover card even when a vertical scrollbar is visible.

Vertical Tabs Scrollbar Alignment: Aligned scrollbar spacing between pinned and unpinned vertical tabs to prevent visual jumping when scrolling through long tab lists.

Settings Subpages on Theme Change: Switching system appearance between light and dark mode now keeps you on your current Chrome Settings subpage instead of resetting to the main Settings menu.

Launcher “New Window” Shortcut: Right-clicking or long-pressing Chrome in the app launcher or taskbar now shows a “New Window” shortcut, including when Incognito mode is disabled by enterprise policies.

Google Slides External Monitor Selection: Restored the external monitor picker in Google Slides presentation settings for dual-screen presentations with presenter view and speaker notes.

Close Third-Party Sign-In Prompts: Clicking the close (X) button on third-party Google Sign-In prompts (such as on Reddit) now cleanly dismisses the dialog without freezing.

Partial Translate in PDFs: Selecting text inside PDFs opened in Chrome tabs now shows the Partial Translate option in the right-click menu.

Opening Downloaded PDFs: Clicking a downloaded PDF in Chrome’s download manager now opens it directly in a new browser tab instead of an external system viewer.

Media Controls During Picture-in-Picture: Opening a Picture-in-Picture video window no longer causes the media controls popup in the toolbar to close early.

Web App Installation Window: Installing a window’s only open tab as a web app now opens a New Tab Page instead of leaving an empty browser window.

Web App Back Navigation: Newly opened web app windows now start with only in-app history so the back button no longer returns to pages visited before the app was installed.

Multiple Web Apps on the Same Site: Installing one web app from a site no longer causes other web apps on that same site to appear as “Already installed” or fail to open.

Address Bar Copy Selection: Right-clicking highlighted text in the address bar now opens copy options without clearing your URL selection.

Shift+Up/Down Text Selection in Address Bar: Pressing Shift+Up or Shift+Down while typing in the address bar now extends multi-line text selection instead of selecting search suggestions.

Address Bar Right-Click Menu: Right-clicking anywhere in the address bar now displays the standard desktop text-editing menu.

Ctrl+L Full URL Selection: Pressing Ctrl+L now reveals and selects the complete web address, including URL parameters.

Address Bar Suggestions Dismissal: Clicking outside the address bar now cleanly closes the suggestions dropdown so the search box doesn’t remain stuck open.

Contextual Search Privacy Notice: Contextual search now shows a non-blocking privacy notice instead of a pop-up dialog that interrupts your workflow.

Stability fixes: Stability improvements were made across browser extensions, keyboard shortcuts, and managed browser policies.

title: Everything new in iOS 27.3 beta 2
snippet: iOS 27.3 beta 2 is here. Apple’s next iPhone software update brings a ton of changes including the redesigned Health app and much more. Below, we’re collecting the new features and changes discovered during testing. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.3 beta 2 is here. Apple’s next iPhone software update brings a ton of changes including the redesigned Health app and much more. Below, we’re collecting the new features and changes discovered during testing.

iOS 27.3 beta 2 details

The second iOS 27.3 beta is available for developer beta testers. 

To update, open Settings, tap General, then Software Update. Choose iOS 27 Developer Beta under Beta Updates.

A public beta will likely follow in the days to come.

Here’s what’s new in the new iOS 27.3 beta 2 release:

iPhone Duo can now be unlocked with facial recognition (with limitations). Details here.

iPhone Duo includes a new option to lock the phone when closing from unfolded state. The setting is added to Display & Brightness in Settings app.

Calendar app has been redesigned with new bottom-oriented controls. Details here.

macOS Full Disk Access permissions have been updated. Details here.

Apple TV app adds video podcasts section. There’s also a new vertical video feature. Details here.

Siri AI gains ability to answer health-related questions. Details here.

Apple News+ Puzzles offerings expand to Australia, French Canada, and the UK. Puzzle availability varies by region.

Siri AI can now use an entire webpage in Safari for context. This works with content that isn’t in view as well.

Siri AI comes to Apple TV 4K (second- and third-gen) in tvOS 27.3 beta 2

Prior to iOS 27.3 beta 2, these changes were included:

Redesigned Health app returns in beta. It was previously previewed in iOS 27.2 beta for a few cycles. Apple signals that it will ship with iOS 27.3 before the end of this year. Details here.

Audio Intelligence features for Apple Watch, including Siri Recap and Live Rewind, are available to beta test in watchOS 27.3 beta with iOS 27.3 beta. Details here.

Apple Fitness+ adds Gym Strength workouts. Details here. 

Safari gains vertical tabs, adaptive dark mode, and more. Details here.

Siri AI language support expands to include Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

iPhone Duo adds Reachability accessibility feature. Originally designed to shift content down the screen on tall displays, iPhone Duo’s version is designed to shift content from the left or right across the display for reaching across wide screens.

iPadOS 27.3 adds support for Siri Mode in the Camera app, plus Visual Intelligence with Apple Pencil support.

StandBy mode on standard iPhone models has been updated to work more like iPhone Duo. For example, digital and analog clock faces are more customizable with options to set up multiple configurations of the same faces with the ability to swipe between options. These are also configurable with various colors and complications, similar to Apple Watch faces.

Siri AI is now able to take actions in apps like Calendar, Journal, Messages, Music, and more. You can ask Siri AI what it can do in supported apps to discover new capabilities. Details here.

Apple Music app splash screen highlights improved Auto Mix, reimagined Artist Pages, and Concerts For you based on listening.

We’ll keep adding discoveries as we spend more time with the update. Have you found a change in iOS 27.3 beta 2? Share it in the comments or email tips@9to5mac.com.

title: Someone rebuilt old Android versions in your browser, and it’s an instant nostalgia hit [Gallery]
snippet: The “Android Time Machine” is a fun project that puts Android versions into your browser, giving you a quick and easy chance to play around with older versions for a quick hit of nostalgia. more…
fullText:
The “Android Time Machine” is a fun project that puts Android versions into your browser, giving you a quick and easy chance to play around with older versions for a quick hit of nostalgia.

Built on the back of AOSP builds for classic Nexus devices, “Android Time Machine” lets you quickly  access older Android versions. Specifically, Android 2.1 Eclair through Android 7.1.2 Nougat. 

The simulator runs within the shell of a matching Nexus smartphone on a desktop browser, or to fit your actual smartphone if you run it on Android. 

Versions and simulated smartphones include:

	

Android 2.1 Eclair: Nexus One

Android 2.3.6 Gingerbread: Nexus S

Android 4.0.4 Ice Cream Sandwich: Galaxy Nexus

Android 4.3 Jelly Bean: Nexus 4

Android 4.4.4 KitKat: Nexus 5

Android 5.1.1 Lollipop: Nexus 6

Android 6.0.1 Marshmallow: Nexus 5X

Android 7.1.2 Nougat: Nexus 6P

The best part here is how it works on your actual smartphone. When launched in fullscreen, it  scales to match your phone’s screen – meaning it fits even devices like the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s smaller outer display (it just shows the desktop version when open). 

Since this is running through the browser and not an actual Android build, you won’t get a perfect replication. Performance is a little hit or miss, especially with certain animations, but it works really well overall. 

The browser even simulates results from each era (oh, to go back to when Google Search wasn’t an absolute mess). Similarly, Google apps and the camera are filled with placeholders since the web app can’t access the actual camera or connect to the internet to sign into a Google account.

Seeing things like the boot animations and live wallpapers from classic Nexus phones, as well as peeking back at lost apps like Google+ and Play Music, is just such a fun little piece of nostalgia. 

“Android Time Machine” is free, and the source code is available on GitHub.

fullText:

Google’s Gemini-powered Intelligent Eyewear lineup launched last week with collections from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, with pricing starting at $395. Just a few days later, though, over half of the lineup is sold out.

title: Critical Java Flaw Leaves Systems Open to Hackers
snippet: The Java4Shell vulnerability could allow hackers to take over systems without a password.
fullText:
A newly identified vulnerability in Oracle Java could give hackers unauthorized access to major applications and allow them to run code without logging in. The flaw could affect a sweeping array of big businesses, including tech companies like Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple and Netflix, which rely heavily on Java’s server-side software and core products.

“Roughly 90% of Fortune 500 companies run on Java,” Thai Duong, CEO of cybersecurity firm Calif, said. 

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 (and dubbed Java4Shell), corrupts memory when Java decodes Base64, a standard format used to transmit login credentials and file uploads.

			

More from CNET

Duong told CNET that his company identified the critical software vulnerability in October and notified Oracle, which has since patched the vulnerability. This week, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued guidance urging organizations to do the same immediately. CISA recommends identifying affected Java installations, reviewing software inventory for JDKs and Java runtimes, and applying vendor patches as soon as they’re available.

Oracle rated the flaw a serious 8.1 out of 10 on the standard vulnerability scale. It can lead to an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Java, allowing hackers to run their own malicious commands or code over the internet without requiring a username, password or prior access. 

Federico Kirschbaum, head of Security Lab, the research arm at cybersecurity company XBOW, told CNET that Java is primarily used at the enterprise level. As a result, the vulnerability could trickle across different sectors, including finance, government, transportation and large corporations.

“Java is a great language for creating solutions, but this vulnerability — it’s a reminder that maybe the languages that we’re using have flaws, and everything built on those might inherit that problem,” Kirschbaum said. 

Amid recent technological disruptions, he suggested leaning on AI solutions to address vulnerabilities in AI.

“That new normal is that most of the technology we rely on has flaws, and now that we have resources using LLMs, we can find those problems,” Kirschbaum said. 

He pointed out that bad actors and hackers can also find these vulnerabilities.

“We are in a race to find the problems first and help the industry by guiding them on what’s urgent so they patch it,” Kirschbaum said.

title: Google Wallet may soon be able to store your Social Security card
snippet: Google Wallet is preparing another form of digital ID storage, with support for your Social Security card apparently on the way. more…
fullText:
Google Wallet is preparing another form of digital ID storage, with support for your Social Security card apparently on the way.

You can already store your passport or select State driver’s licenses in Google Wallet in the US, and it seems Google isn’t stopping there. Wallet now appears to be preparing some level of support for storing a digital copy of your Social Security card, as code in the latest app updates suggest.

The folks over at Android Authority spotted explicit references to “Social Security Number” in Google Play Services v26.46.30 in connection with Google Wallet.

<string name=”pay_id_uhura_visible_name”>Social Security Number</string>

While exact functionality is unclear at this time, this appears to include support for seeing your Social Security benefits, or at least logging those benefits, in a digital form. There are mentions of Retirement, Survivors, and/or Disability Insurance (RSDI), Supplemental Security Income, Medicare, and more, as well as qualifiers for deductions and effective dates.

	

Would you find this useful?

fullText:
Update, 6:15 p.m. ET: Apple has now released beta 2 for tvOS 27.3 (24K5298d) and HomePod 27.3 (24K5298d).

Apple has just released beta 2 for iPadOS 27.3, watchOS 27.3, visionOS 27.3, and more. It’s available for developers, but a public beta will likely follow in the next couple days.

Developer beta 2 is here for iPadOS 27.3 and more

Two weeks ago Apple introduced an exciting wave of beta updates as iOS 27.3 and companion releases introduced many new features.

Siri AI upgrades are a big focus in 27.3, with new languages, Siri Recap, and advanced in-app actions. There’s also a preview of new third-party app capabilities for Siri.

The all-new Health app has returned in iOS and iPadOS 27.3, this time with the expectation of launching in the public release. Fitness also adds a new Gym Strength program.

Apple Music now has a Selfie Sing feature for creating personal karaoke videos, and an improved lyrics view. Safari adds Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and more.

That’s just a sampling of the new features in beta 1. And now today, beta 2 is here for iPadOS 27.3, watchOS 27.3, visionOS 27.3, and more.

We’re expecting to see additional new features and refinements today, like video podcasts being added to the Apple TV app. We’ll keep you posted on everything noteworthy we discover.

watchOS 27.3 has one of my personal favorite new features in Siri Recap, so I’m curious to see if Apple keeps refining the experience throughout the beta in response to user feedback.

title: Palmer Luckey thinks China is ‘thrilled to have Jensen out,’ so he wants the ousted Nvidia CEO reinstated
snippet: "It makes America weaker to knock him out," the Anduril CEO said about ousted Nvidia leader Jensen Huang.
fullText:
Image Credits:PATRICK T. FALLON/AFP / Getty Images	

	

						

1:31 PM PST · November 18, 2026

											

			

Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey thinks Nvidia’s board is giving China exactly what it wants by removing the company’s longtime CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang.

Nvidia, the leading semiconductor designer whose chips power much of the AI industry, is undergoing a critical, unexpected leadership change. Huang, who led the company for 33 years, stepped down last week amid several controversies, including his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy who has been investigated for possibly smuggling Nvidia chips into China to circumvent U.S. export restrictions.

“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, repeating a statement he posted on X last week. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out.”

Luckey disagrees with Huang’s longstanding position that Nvidia should have more leeway to export chips to China. But he also recognizes that China stands to benefit if its  domestic chipmakers can challenge Nvidia’s dominance.

“China doesn’t want Nvidia to sell GPUs to Chinese companies,” Luckey said. “There are Chinese companies that want to buy Nvidia GPUs… China will not give them an import permit because they want to build an internal domestic processor industry… not build one that is dependent on the United States.”

Nvidia has said as much itself — the U.S. government granted the company license to ship some of its powerful H200 chips to certain Chinese customers, but those sales were restricted by the Chinese government. Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress said during the company’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday that it will no longer sell H200 chips in China at all.

Luckey is far from alone among industry peers in his defense of Huang. 

More than 200,000 people — including Elon Musk and the CEOs of Y Combinator, Databricks, Epic Games, Shopify, and Replit — have signed a petition calling for Nvidia to reinstate its founder. But Nvidia executives said during the company’s earnings call on Tuesday that the company does not have plans to reappoint Huang, even though the founder offered to return.

title: Instagram finally lets users edit Stories after publishing, but there’s a catch
snippet: Every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days. more…
fullText:
Every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days.

No more deleting and reposting Stories

As spotted by The Verge, Instagram head Adam Mosseri confirmed today that the app will finally let users edit a Story after publishing.

This means users will be able to add stickers and drawings, fix typos or adjust text, and even change the music without having to delete the Story and publish it again, which would mean losing any views it had already received.

The catch is that users will only have 15 minutes after publishing a Story to make changes by tapping the ellipsis button at the bottom of the screen, and then selecting “Edit story.”

Here’s Mosseri’s post announcing the news:

Today’s update is the latest in a series of changes Instagram has made this year to address longstanding user requests.

Back in March, the app introduced the ability to reorder photos and videos in a carousel after publishing. In April, it added an option to edit comments (also within 15 minutes of posting), and in June, it began letting users manually rearrange posts on their profile grid.

More recently, Instagram also brought its free Edits video editor to the Mac, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, and 4K exports.

snippet: There are rumors of a Samsung phone with an “extremely bezel-less” display coming from one of the company’s suppliers, and it might be on one of the next Galaxy S27 models. more…
fullText:
There are rumors of a Samsung phone with an “extremely bezel-less” display coming from one of the company’s suppliers, and it might be on one of the next Galaxy S27 models.

The information comes from a related supplier for Samsung and was brought up by a known leaker, Lanzuk. Their Naver post specifically mentions an “extremely bezel-less” display. What that means is up for debate, and machine translation does not clarify the original post in Korean.

The big takeaway might be that Samsung is looking to launch one of these bezel-less display options within the Galaxy S27 lineup. An early adoption might indicate that even though this supplier planned on developing these displays for an upcoming Galaxy device, Samsung may want to push the timeline forward and fit it to one of the Galaxy S27 series phones.

Which device would debut a new “extremely bezel-less” display is up in the air. Odds are it would be the most expensive option’s display that gets updated – the Galaxy S27 Ultra. It’s also possible it could show up on both the Pro and Ultra variants, to stretch the premium tag across the upper end of the lineup.

	

This leak is probably best taken with a grain of salt. The author seems to have doubts, and this seems like a 50/50 shot. But even if Samsung doesn’t shave the bezels off of one of the Galaxy S27 models, this leak still indicates a future device will get a similar display.

That previously planned iteration may even be a better version than anything the Galaxy S27 series could have. More than a proof-of-concept.

The Galaxy S27 series is expected to launch early next year. In the meantime, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is nearly bezel-less, folds, and is marked down at its best price for the holidays.

title: At Scout Motors’ New Plant, Validation of Terra and Traveler EVs Has Begun
snippet: Early preproduction Terra trucks and Traveler SUVs are coming together at the Blythewood Production Center. I got an inside look.
fullText:
At Scout Motors’ South Carolina Production Center, the automaker’s very first electrified trucks and SUVs are being welded, painted and assembled. The revived American automaker has begun the first validation builds of its upcoming Terra pickup truck and Traveler SUV at the Blythewood plant, but hold your electric horses — final production and customer deliveries are still a little over a year away.

After a period of slow sales, American interest in electric vehicles and hybrids is on the rise, driven by high fuel costs and the steady growth of EV charging infrastructure in 2026. Scout, with its battery-electric and gasoline range-extended powertrains, could have both of those bases covered when it arrives to compete in America’s most popular vehicle classes (trucks and SUVs) in 2028. It’s worth keeping an eye on Scout as it inches toward production.

I donned my hardhat, steel-toe caps and high-vis vest to get an early look inside the plant.

			

More from CNET

The road so far

The Volkswagen Group revived the Scout Motors brand (formerly International Scout) in 2022, and in 2024, the public got its first look at the Terra and Traveler concepts. The two were initially revealed as full-electric models with the option to add Scout’s Harvester onboard gasoline generator to boost the range. 

However, demand for the extended-range EV configuration was overwhelming — roughly 87% of the 160,000-plus reservation holders selected the Harvester spec over the all-electric version — and Scout pivoted to delivering the EREV first, then following up with the pure battery-electric model later in production. 

Scout’s vehicles were initially announced as EVs, but the Harvester range extender proved to be more popular.Scout Motors

Both models are expected to start under $60,000, though Scout has not yet confirmed the exact price difference between the Harvester and pure BEV trims.

In early 2024, the automaker broke ground on the Blythewood Production Center, pledging to invest more than $2 billion in the plant and create more than 4,000 local jobs. A year later, Scout announced plans to add a $300 million supplier park to the complex, supporting around 1,000 on-site jobs at parts suppliers.

Today, construction is mostly complete. (Executives told me it’s about 80% to 95% done, depending on how you measure it.) The walls are up, much of the equipment is in place, and the first movement toward full production of the brand’s extended-range EV and, eventually, battery electric trucks and SUVs has begun.

What’s happening in South Carolina

Scout’s manufacturing and production teams have begun building the first validation builds — early-stage preproduction vehicles that allow factory planners to dial in vehicle quality, confirm the accuracy of the engineering and hone the efficiency of the manufacturing and assembly lines. 

These aren’t complete vehicles by any stretch, being pulled from the line at various points to check and double-check that the new factory equipment functions properly and that the right parts arrive when and where they’re needed. Executives warned me that, at this point, there would still be inconsistencies as they dial in panel gaps, welds and the application of various coatings, but that Scout expects the process to be dialed in by the time full production starts in late 2027.

During my visit, robotic arms went through the motions, but no vehicles were being welded. Scout Motors

I was able to get up close to these validation vehicles, checking out a body-in-white bare chassis in the body shop, seeing various stages of coatings applied to bare metal, and watching workers complete calibration and alignment of lights and sensors in the final assembly area. 

Along the way, Scout told me that more than 160 individual parts must come together to form the vehicle’s chassis, a process supported by more than 750 robots and 5,000 weld points. Once up to speed, the factory body shop is designed to produce around 40 vehicles per hour, with pickups and SUVs sharing the same line.

However, while I saw the robotic welding arms and paint sprayers performing their motions to apply color, no vehicles were actually moving through the assembly line. This early in the process, the automaker doesn’t need a continuous flow of validation vehicles, and many of the factory areas — such as the supplier park that will provide the batteries, electric motors and modified VW Group four-cylinder engines for Harvester models — are still under construction. 

What’s next?

Additionally, the validation process gives workers hands-on experience, rather than having them learn from mistakes on cars that will reach customers or being confined to a classroom.

As more parts of the factory complete construction and come online, the validation process will encompass more of the vehicle’s construction until the automaker is ready to start building full customer vehicles. Todd Johnson, Scout’s vice president of manufacturing, tells me that validation will continue into 2027 through multiple preproduction phases starting with the Traveler SUV. 

The automaker expects the first customer deliveries of the Traveler Harvester to begin in early 2028, followed by the Terra Harvester and, eventually, fully electric versions of both.

Editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Scout Motors. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

							Senior Writer, Electrified Cars

The revived American automaker has begun the first validation builds of its upcoming Terra pickup truck and Traveler SUV at the Blythewood plant, but hold your electric horses — final production and customer deliveries are still a little over a year away.

After a period of slow sales, American interest in electric vehicles and hybrids is on the rise, driven by high fuel costs and the steady growth of EV charging infrastructure in 2026. Scout, with its battery-electric and gasoline range-extended powertrains, could have both of those bases covered when it arrives to compete in America’s most popular vehicle classes (trucks and SUVs) in 2028. It’s worth keeping an eye on Scout as it inches toward production.

title: Phone by Google 246 rolls out gradient icon redesign on Android [U]
snippet: Following the Messages update earlier this week, Phone by Google has received its redesigned gradient icon in the beta channel. more…
fullText:

By leveraging gradients for the earpiece and mouthpiece, the new design feels flatter and lighter than the old one. Additionally, the darker blue shade has been removed entirely. Google says the “app icon is now crisper, clearer, and designed to look sharp on your home screen.”

We also refreshed the coloring, spacing, and gradients to bring the icon closer in line with the modern look of the rest of the Google ecosystem. Now, the Phone app blends seamlessly with all your other Google tools, making your screen feel cohesive and clean.

There are no other changes to the app with this update. Zooming out, Google has yet to roll out the restored Contacts tab to stable users as of today.

title: Siri Modular Apple Watch face gains two new styles with watchOS 27.3
snippet: Siri Modular, the new Apple Watch face in watchOS 27, is gaining new style options. watchOS 27.3, currently in beta, adds two more style options to the existing set. This gives users five options for adjusting what type of information appears on Siri Modular. more…
fullText:
Siri Modular, the new Apple Watch face in watchOS 27, is gaining new style options. watchOS 27.3, currently in beta, adds two more style options to the existing set. This gives users five options for adjusting what type of information appears on Siri Modular. 

watchOS 27.3 adds two Siri-focused styles to Siri Modular

Siri Modular originally shipped with three style options. Each supports a small line complication above the time. 

Additionally, the original three styles include these options:

Large digital click + three circular complications

Compact digital clock + Smart Stack tile + three circular complications 

Large digital clock + Smart Stack tile

In watchOS 27.3, Apple introduces two new Siri features that work with Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.

First, there’s Siri Recap which uses the Apple Watch to turn audio into high-level text summaries. Second, there’s Live Rewind which lets you view a transcript of the last 15 seconds of spoken word.

The two new Siri Modular Apple Watch face styles help surface three things: invoking Siri, viewing conversations with Siri, and viewing Siri Recaps on the Apple Watch.

The new styles include a pill-shaped module that includes icon shortcuts that go directly to Siri conversations, invoke Siri AI, or go directly to Siri Recaps in the Siri app.

One style features a large digital clock with the new three-button Siri module. Another includes a compact digital clock with a Smart Stack tile and the new three-button Siri module.

This brings the style options to five. If you use the three circular complications configuration, you can also assign a Siri icon that invokes Siri AI. 

watchOS 27.3 is currently in beta and expected to be released officially in December.
